prompt.context: Your client is Canyon Capital Partners (CCP). CCP is a long-established hedge fund headquartered in Hartford, CT. Hedge funds make money mainly out of management fees and carried interests. Over the past two years, CCP's profits have been declining. Its CEO and founder has hired you to help her understand why profits are trending down and what she should do to restore the firm to a more profitable route.
prompt.question: Why are CCP's profits declining, and what should the CEO do to restore the firm to a more profitable path?

clarifying_info.a: They manage investors' money to generate above-market investment returns. CCP only invests in US public equity markets.

clarifying_info.q: How much money does CCP manage?
clarifying_info.a: Current assets under management (AuM) are $2.1 billion. In the past three years, the fund has not had any new inflows or outflows of investor money.
Fixed fees paid on the average balance of assets under management. CCP's management fees were 2.0% per year but were reduced to 1.5% since 2016 because of competitive pressure.
Share of investment performance appropriated by the fund's managers as additional compensation. CCP takes 20% of all investment gains in excess of the 15% hurdle rate in the year.

exhibits.title: AuM & Investment Performance
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis chart showing Assets under Management (AuM in $mm, left axis) and Investment Performance (%, right axis) across 2015, 2016, and 2017.
exhibits.data: AuM rises from approximately $1,500mm to $2,100mm over the three years; Investment Performance was roughly 20% in 2015, 5% in 2016, and 0% in 2017.

exhibits.title: Employee Headcount
exhibits.shows: A table showing headcount by employee category (C-Suite, Portfolio Managers, Associates, Analysts, Traders, Support Staff) for 2015, 2016, and 2017.
exhibits.data: C-Suite: 3/3/3; Portfolio Managers: 3/3/4; Associates: 7/10/16; Analysts: 13/11/9; Traders: 3/3/3; Support Staff: 7/8/9.

framework: Revenues: Management Fees (driven by AuM level and fee rate) and Carried Interests (driven by investment performance vs. hurdle rate)
Costs: Employee Compensation (headcount and salary structure), Office Rent, Research Materials
External context (not primary focus): Regulation, Competition, Market Trends

questions.prompt: Calculate total revenues for 2015, 2016, and 2017 using Exhibit 1.
questions.guidance: Strong answer walks through both revenue lines year by year. Management Fee Revenue = Average AuM × Fee Rate. Carried Interest = 20% of returns above the 15% hurdle. Candidate should spot that management fee revenue fell due to the rate cut in 2016, and carried interest dropped to zero in 2016 and 2017 due to sub-hurdle performance.

math.setup: Management Fee Revenue = Average AuM ($mm) × Management Fee (%); Carried Interest = (Total Return − AuM × 15%) × 20% when positive, else $0
steps: 2015: Mgmt Fee = $1,600mm × 2.00% = $32.0mm; Total Return = $1,500mm × 20% = $300mm; Excess = $300mm − $1,500mm × 15% = $300mm − $225mm = $75mm; Carried Interest = $75mm × 20% = $15.0mm; Total = $47.0mm
2016: Mgmt Fee = $1,800mm × 1.50% = $27.0mm; Investment performance 5% < 15% hurdle; Carried Interest = $0; Total = $27.0mm
2017: Mgmt Fee = $1,900mm × 1.50% = $28.5mm; Investment performance 0% < 15% hurdle; Carried Interest = $0; Total = $28.5mm
math.answer: Total Revenues: 2015 = $47.0mm, 2016 = $27.0mm, 2017 = $28.5mm. Revenue fell $20mm from 2015 to 2016, driven by fee rate cut (−$5mm) and loss of carried interest (−$15mm).

questions.prompt: Analyze cost trends using Exhibit 2 and the salary information provided when asked.
questions.guidance: Candidate should notice total headcount is rising and that the mix is shifting: Associates (higher cost than Analysts) are growing rapidly while Analysts are being replaced. Should calculate total salary cost each year and compare against revenues.

math.setup: Total Salary = Sum of (headcount × annual salary) for each category. C-Suite $1,500,000; Portfolio Managers $500,000; Associates $250,000; Analysts $100,000; Traders $200,000; Support Staff $75,000.
steps: 2015: C-Suite 3×$1.5mm=$4.5mm; PM 3×$0.5mm=$1.5mm; Assoc 7×$0.25mm=$1.75mm; Analysts 13×$0.1mm=$1.3mm; Traders 3×$0.2mm=$0.6mm; Support 7×$0.075mm=$0.525mm; Total=$10.175mm
2016: C-Suite $4.5mm; PM $1.5mm; Assoc 10×$0.25mm=$2.5mm; Analysts 11×$0.1mm=$1.1mm; Traders $0.6mm; Support 8×$0.075mm=$0.6mm; Total=$10.8mm
2017: C-Suite $4.5mm; PM 4×$0.5mm=$2.0mm; Assoc 16×$0.25mm=$4.0mm; Analysts 9×$0.1mm=$0.9mm; Traders $0.6mm; Support 9×$0.075mm=$0.675mm; Total=$12.675mm
math.answer: Total Salary: 2015=$10.175mm, 2016=$10.8mm, 2017=$12.675mm. Costs rose ~$2.5mm while revenues fell ~$18.5mm over the period. Key driver: Associates (cost $250K each) are replacing lower-cost Analysts ($100K each).

questions.prompt: What is driving the headcount mix shift (associates rising, analysts declining), and why does it matter?
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize that associates are more expensive than analysts and that hiring more associates while cutting analysts increases the cost per unit of research output. Office rent and research material costs are stable and immaterial to the analysis.

recommendation: Increase revenues: (1) Raise the management fee back toward 2.0% or explore tiered fee structures; (2) Grow AuM through a new fundraising round targeting institutional investors; (3) Implement new investment strategies or improve portfolio management to exceed the 15% hurdle rate and restore carried interest income.

Reduce costs: (1) Promote a meritocracy-based turnover policy to rebalance the associate/analyst ratio; (2) Reduce the number of associates and increase the number of analysts to lower per-capita compensation cost while maintaining research capacity.
risks: Raising the management fee may scare off existing investors or make CCP less competitive in the market.
Letting go of associates could hurt employee morale and damage the firm's ability to attract talent.
Reducing headcount may constrain future growth if AuM expands significantly.
next_steps: Develop a strategy and timeline for a new round of fundraising to grow AuM.
Identify which associates to transition out; establish transparent rules for employee turnover and promotion based on performance.
